text:
ana: Trying a proposal: implement a "fast-restore probe" for on-prem bootstraps so a node can become "available" quickly while the rest of payloads stream in the background. Thoughts?
kevin: interesting. by "available" you mean accept lightweight RPCs vs full inference traffic?
maria: yeah, minimal surface: runtime binary, operator config, model index + first N shards, and attestation keys. verify signatures, then flip availability. heavier shards and KV cache fetch async.
rahul: big tradeoffs: exposes app to cold-start tail latency and potential degraded accuracy if missing shards. need request gating for ops that require full model state.
nana: small nit: my name is ana ;)
nana: also: we need clear operator controls: how to choose N (warmup_shards), and a safety timer to revert to full-sync if background fetch stalls.
kevin: agree. propose config example to make it concrete:
```
bootstrap:
  strategy: fast-restore
  require_signatures: true
  warmup_shards: 2   # number of model shards to activate synchronously
  deferred_fetch: true
  background_timeout: 10m
  behavior_on_missing_critical: block
```
maria: +1. also add a probe endpoint that reports per-component verified status so SRE/ops can see which shards are pending. e.g. `GET /-/bootstrap/status`.
rahul: operational safety: if a node flips available but misses an operator-mandated compliance artifact (e.g. a signed policy), we should refuse activation. differentiate critical vs optional artifacts.
nana: for air-gapped installs, we must not assume external mirrors. background fetch will be local copy or operator-led sidecar pull. define two fetch modes: local (sidecar pulls from operator bastion) vs peer (other nodes).
kevin: peer fetch is nice for speed but raises integrity complexity: need per-chunk signatures or chunked Merkle proofs so node can verify pieces as they arrive.
maria: suggested integrity model: manifest with component-level signatures + manifest-level root signature. allow partial activation if all items marked "critical" are present and verified.
rahul: fallback policy: if background fetch fails or stalls beyond background_timeout, either (a) automatically enqueue full-graph re-sync and throttle traffic, or (b) demote node to degraded and remove from LB. operator picks default.
deploy-bot: rollout plan: canary the behavior with 5% of dedicated nodes, monitor error rate and 95th token latency. auto-rollback after 15m threshold breach.
nana: UX: `rictl bootstrap inspect <node>` should show: verified components, pending list, bytes pulled/sec, last-verified-hash, and recommended action. also ability to `rictl bootstrap pause/force-complete` for operator intervention.
kevin: one more concern: model version pinning. if fast-restore activates with a subset of shards from version X, background fetch must ensure remaining shards are the same commit. otherwise we need to abort activation.
maria: implement background fetch with a single commit-id and verify chunk manifests reference that id. if mismatch, mark node inconsistent and trigger rollback.
rahul: final safety idea: soft-quarantine window: node accepts only internal health probes for X minutes after activation, while LB adds it to warm pool rather than full traffic. prevents client-facing regressions.
nana: action items: 1) write lightweight RFC describing probe endpoints + manifest signature format (maria). 2) prototype `bootstrap.strategy=fast-restore` in onprem operator (kevin). 3) small UX additions to rictl (rahul). 4) define rollout guardrails (deploy-bot + SRE).
maria: I'll draft RFC with example manifests and threat model by EOD Friday.
kevin: happy to pick up prototype after RFC.
rahul: I'll own rictl sketches and the warm-pool LB semantics.
nana: thanks all, this feels like a good directional approach. :+1:
